True Statement: Cereals such as wheat, rice, maize, millets and sorghum provide us carbohydrates for energy.
False 1: Pulses such as wheat, rice, maize, millets and sorghum provide us carbohydrates for energy.

True Statement: Pulses like gram, pea, black gram, green gram, pigeon pea and lentil provide us with protein.
False 1: Oilseeds like gram, pea, black gram, green gram, pigeon pea and lentil provide us with protein.

True Statement: Oilseeds including soyabean, groundnut, sesame, castor, mustard, linseed and sunflower provide us with necessary fats.
False 1: Pulses including soyabean, groundnut, sesame, castor, mustard, linseed and sunflower provide us with necessary fats.

True Statement: Kharif crops are grown from June to October; examples include paddy, soyabean, pigeon pea, maize, cotton, green gram and black gram.
False 1: Rabi crops are grown from June to October; examples include paddy, soyabean, pigeon pea, maize, cotton, green gram and black gram.

True Statement: Rabi crops are grown from November to April; examples include wheat, gram, peas, mustard and linseed.
False 1: Kharif crops are grown from November to April; examples include wheat, gram, peas, mustard and linseed.

True Statement: India achieved a four times increase in food grain production from 1952 to 2010 with only 25% increase in the cultivable land area.
False 1: India achieved a four times increase in food grain production from 1952 to 2010 with only 50% increase in the cultivable land area.

True Statement: Hybridisation refers to crossing between genetically dissimilar plants; it may be intervarietal, interspecific or intergeneric.
False 1: Hybridisation refers to crossing between genetically similar plants; it may be intervarietal, interspecific or intergeneric.

True Statement: Genetically modified crops are obtained by introducing a gene that would provide the desired characteristic into the crop.
False 1: Hybridised crops are obtained by introducing a gene that would provide the desired characteristic.

True Statement: Photoperiods are related to the duration of sunlight; growth of plants and flowering are dependent on sunlight.
False 1: Photoperiods are related to the intensity of sunlight; growth of plants and flowering are independent of sunlight.

True Statement: Nutrients are supplied to plants by air, water and soil; air supplies carbon and oxygen, water supplies hydrogen, and soil supplies the other thirteen nutrients.
False 1: Nutrients are supplied to plants by air, water and soil; air supplies nitrogen and carbon, water supplies oxygen, and soil supplies thirteen nutrients.

True Statement: Macronutrients are required by plants in large quantities; micronutrients are required in small quantities.
False 1: Micronutrients are required by plants in large quantities; macronutrients are required in small quantities.

True Statement: The macronutrients supplied by soil are nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium, magnesium and sulphur.
False 1: The micronutrients supplied by soil are nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium, magnesium and sulphur.

True Statement: Manure is prepared by the decomposition of animal excreta and plant waste; it contains large quantities of organic matter and supplies small quantities of nutrients.
False 1: Fertilizers are prepared by the decomposition of animal excreta and plant waste; they contain large quantities of organic matter and supply small quantities of nutrients.

True Statement: Compost is prepared by decomposing farm waste material like livestock excreta, vegetable waste, domestic waste and straw in pits.
False 1: Vermi-compost is prepared by decomposing farm waste material in pits without earthworms.

True Statement: Vermi-compost is compost prepared by using earthworms to hasten the process of decomposition of plant and animal refuse.
False 1: Vermi-compost is compost prepared by using bacteria to hasten the process of decomposition of plant and animal refuse.

True Statement: Green manure is made by growing plants like sun hemp or guar and then ploughing them into the soil; it enriches the soil in nitrogen and phosphorus.
False 1: Green manure is made by growing plants like sun hemp or guar and then ploughing them into the soil; it enriches the soil in potassium and calcium.

True Statement: Fertilizers are commercially produced plant nutrients that supply nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.
False 1: Manures are commercially produced plant nutrients that supply nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.

True Statement: Organic farming is a farming system with minimal or no use of chemicals as fertilizers, herbicides and pesticides, and with maximum input of organic manures and recycled farm-wastes.
False 1: Intensive farming is a farming system with minimal or no use of chemicals as fertilizers, herbicides and pesticides, and with maximum input of organic manures and recycled farm-wastes.

True Statement: Mixed cropping is growing two or more crops simultaneously on the same piece of land; examples are wheat + gram, or wheat + mustard, or groundnut + sunflower.
False 1: Inter-cropping is growing two or more crops simultaneously on the same piece of land; examples are wheat + gram, or wheat + mustard, or groundnut + sunflower.

True Statement: Inter-cropping is growing two or more crops simultaneously on the same field in a definite pattern; examples are soyabean + maize, or finger millet + cowpea.
False 1: Mixed cropping is growing two or more crops simultaneously on the same field in a definite pattern; examples are soyabean + maize, or finger millet + cowpea.

True Statement: In inter-cropping, crops are selected such that their nutrient requirements are different, ensuring maximum utilisation of the nutrients supplied and preventing spread of pests and diseases.
False 1: In mixed cropping, crops are selected such that their nutrient requirements are different, ensuring maximum utilisation of the nutrients supplied and preventing spread of pests and diseases.

True Statement: Crop rotation is the growing of different crops on a piece of land in a pre-planned succession.
False 1: Intercropping is the growing of different crops on a piece of land in a pre-planned succession.

True Statement: Weeds are unwanted plants in cultivated fields; they compete for food, space and light and take up nutrients, reducing the growth of the crop.
False 1: Insect pests are unwanted plants in cultivated fields; they compete for food, space and light and take up nutrients.

True Statement: Diseases in plants are caused by pathogens such as bacteria, fungi and viruses, which can be present in and transmitted through soil, water and air.
False 1: Diseases in plants are caused only by fungi, which are transmitted through soil only.

True Statement: Generally insect pests attack plants by cutting the root, stem and leaf; sucking cell sap from various parts; or boring into stem and fruits.
False 1: Generally insect pests attack plants by only one method: sucking cell sap from various parts of the plant.

True Statement: Storage losses in agricultural produce are caused by biotic factors such as insects, rodents, fungi, mites and bacteria, and abiotic factors such as inappropriate moisture and temperatures.
False 1: Storage losses in agricultural produce are caused only by biotic factors such as insects, rodents, fungi, mites and bacteria; abiotic factors do not cause storage losses.

True Statement: The green revolution contributed to increased food-grain production; the white revolution led to better and more efficient availability of milk.
False 1: The white revolution contributed to increased food-grain production; the green revolution led to better and more efficient availability of milk.

True Statement: Animal husbandry is the scientific management of animal livestock including various aspects such as feeding, breeding and disease control.
False 1: Cattle husbandry is the scientific management of all animal livestock including various aspects such as feeding, breeding and disease control.

True Statement: Indian cattle belong to two species: Bos indicus (cows) and Bos bubalis (buffaloes).
False 1: Indian cattle belong to two species: Bos taurus (cows) and Bos indicus (buffaloes).

True Statement: Milk-producing female cattle are called milch (dairy) animals; those used for farm labour such as tilling and carting are called draught animals.
False 1: Milk-producing female cattle are called draught animals; those used for farm labour are called milch animals.

True Statement: Exotic or foreign cattle breeds such as Jersey and Brown Swiss are selected for long lactation periods.
False 1: Local cattle breeds such as Red Sindhi and Sahiwal are selected for long lactation periods.

True Statement: Local cattle breeds such as Red Sindhi and Sahiwal show excellent resistance to diseases.
False 1: Exotic cattle breeds such as Jersey and Brown Swiss show excellent resistance to diseases.

True Statement: The food requirements of dairy animals are of two types: maintenance requirement (food for healthy life) and milk-producing requirement (food during lactation).
False 1: The food requirements of dairy animals are of three types: maintenance requirement, growth requirement and milk-producing requirement.

True Statement: Animal feed includes roughage (largely fibre) and concentrates (low in fibre but with relatively high levels of proteins and other nutrients).
False 1: Animal feed includes roughage (low in fibre, high in proteins) and concentrates (largely fibre).

True Statement: Poultry farming is undertaken to raise domestic fowl for egg production and chicken meat; layers are raised for eggs and broilers are raised for meat.
False 1: Poultry farming is undertaken to raise domestic fowl for egg production and chicken meat; broilers are raised for eggs and layers are raised for meat.

True Statement: Cross-breeding programmes for poultry variety improvement are done between Indian indigenous breeds (such as Aseel) and foreign exotic breeds (such as Leghorn).
False 1: Cross-breeding programmes for poultry variety improvement are done between Indian indigenous breeds (such as Leghorn) and foreign exotic breeds (such as Aseel).

True Statement: The ration for broilers is protein-rich with adequate fat; the level of vitamins A and K is kept high in poultry feeds.
False 1: The ration for layers is protein-rich with adequate fat; the level of vitamins A and K is kept high in broiler poultry feeds.

True Statement: Fish production includes both finned true fish and shellfish such as prawns and molluscs; fish is a cheap source of animal protein.
False 1: Fish production includes only finned true fish; shellfish such as prawns and molluscs are not included.

True Statement: There are two ways of obtaining fish: capture fishing (from natural resources) and culture fishery (fish farming).
False 1: There are two ways of obtaining fish: capture fishing and mariculture, both from natural marine resources.

True Statement: Popular marine fish varieties include pomphret, mackerel, tuna, sardines and Bombay duck; they are caught using fishing nets from fishing boats.
False 1: Popular freshwater fish varieties include pomphret, mackerel, tuna, sardines and Bombay duck; they are caught using fishing nets from fishing boats.

True Statement: Large schools of fish in the open sea are located using satellites and echo-sounders to increase yields.
False 1: Large schools of fish in the open sea are located using submarines and sonar to increase yields.

True Statement: The practice of culturing fish and shellfish in seawater is called mariculture.
False 1: The practice of culturing fish and shellfish in seawater is called aquaculture.

True Statement: In composite fish culture, a combination of five or six fish species with different food habits is used in a single fishpond so that all parts of the pond are used without competition.
False 1: In composite fish culture, a combination of two or three fish species with identical food habits is used in a single fishpond to maximise production.

True Statement: In composite fish culture: Catlas are surface feeders, Rohus feed in the middle zone, Mrigals and Common Carps are bottom feeders, and Grass Carps feed on weeds.
False 1: In composite fish culture: Rohus are surface feeders, Catlas feed in the middle zone, Mrigals and Common Carps are bottom feeders, and Grass Carps feed on weeds.

True Statement: A problem in composite fish culture is that many fish breed only during monsoon; this is overcome by breeding fish in ponds using hormonal stimulation.
False 1: A problem in composite fish culture is that many fish breed only during monsoon; this is overcome by mixing fish from different wild water bodies.

True Statement: The local varieties of bees used for commercial honey production are Apis cerana indica (Indian bee), A. dorsata (rock bee) and A. florae (little bee).
False 1: The local varieties of bees used for commercial honey production are Apis mellifera (Indian bee), A. dorsata (rock bee) and A. florae (little bee).

True Statement: The Italian bee variety A. mellifera is commonly used for commercial honey production because of its high honey collection capacity, less stinging and ability to stay in a given beehive for long periods.
False 1: The Indian bee variety A. cerana indica is commonly used for commercial honey production because of its high honey collection capacity, less stinging and ability to stay in a given beehive for long periods.

True Statement: Pasturage refers to the flowers available to bees for nectar and pollen collection; it determines the quality and taste of the honey.
False 1: Pasturage refers to the water sources available to bees for drinking; it determines the quality and taste of the honey.

True Statement: Bee-keeping needs low investment and is used by farmers as an additional income-generating activity; beehives also provide wax used in medicinal preparations.
False 1: Bee-keeping needs high investment and is only practiced by specialist farmers; beehives provide only honey.
